info.title: Pizza 4P's POS Store Box API
info.description: What a store's edge calls on its cloud: the store-facing `/sync` surface, `/activate` and `/claim`, the two ways a box first comes to hold a credential, and `/.well-known/pos-cell`, which says which cell to ask. Generated from the handlers (ADR-0177). Every failure carries the AIP-193 `ErrorResponse` envelope. Every route but `/.well-known/pos-cell`, which answers from memory, is rate-limited per client before any credential is read.

get.summary: Anyone asks which cell this is and, optionally, where a tenant is homed.

parameters.name: tenant
parameters.description: A tenant slug: 1 to 63 lower-case letters, digits or `-`, not starting or ending with `-`.

200.description: This cell: `cell_id`, `base_url`, `country_alias`, `home_country` and the `directory_version` it answers from. With `tenant`, also `tenant`: the tenant's home `cell_id`, that cell's `base_url`, and whether it is `here`. Never a redirect. May be cached for 60 seconds

404.description: The directory this cell holds does not list the tenant

503.description: This cell is configured for a signed directory and holds none yet, so it can name no tenant's home; ask again later

get.x-public-reason: asked before any credential exists, by a box being set up or by anyone finding a tenant's cell; it says only what the PII-free cell directory says (ADR-0179)

post.summary:
A device exchanges its activation code for a credential (unauthenticated — the code is the
credential). Single-use and deny-by-default, per [`pos_core::activation::redeem`].

requestBody.description: `code`, the activation code from the store's setup sheet, and optionally the `store_id` the box expects to belong to

201.description: Activated: the `device_id`, and the device `credential`, returned this once; the cloud keeps only its hash (ADR-0050)

400.description: The code or the store id is malformed

403.description: Refused: a spent, revoked, unknown or raced code, or one issued for another store, all answer the same. A code whose cell prefix names another cell says so too: a `code` detail `OTHER_CELL`, with the directory's base URL for that cell in the message, or `UNKNOWN_CELL` when the directory does not list it (ADR-0181)

429.description: Too many activation attempts from this client: `Retry-After` says when to try again

503.description: The activation service, or the OS entropy source, is unavailable

post.x-public-reason: a single-use activation code from the store's setup sheet

post.summary: A box opens a claim. Unauthenticated: the box has nothing to authenticate with yet.

201.description: A claim: its `claim_id`, the `user_code` the box shows, the `secret` it keeps to collect with, when it expires, and how often to poll (ADR-0148)

429.description: Too many activation attempts from this client: `Retry-After` says when to try again

503.description: The claim store, or the OS entropy source, is unavailable

post.x-public-reason: nothing: its code works only once the console binds it

post.summary:
A box polls for its credential. `202` while nobody has bound the code, the credential once it
has, `409` with reason `EXPIRED` when the hour is over, and one `403` for everything else.

parameters.name: claim_id
parameters.description: The claim the box opened, a ULID

requestBody.description: `secret`, the one the claim was opened with

200.description: Bound: the box's `tenant_id`, `store_id` and `device_id`, and its device `credential`, returned this once

202.description: Nobody has bound the code yet: `status` is `PENDING`, and the box asks again

403.description: This claim cannot be collected. Every such refusal answers the same, so it reveals nothing

409.description: The claim has expired (`EXPIRED`): open a new one

429.description: Too many collection polls from this client: `Retry-After` says when to try again

503.description: The claim store, or the OS entropy source, is unavailable

post.x-public-reason: the secret the claim was opened with

post.summary: `POST /sync/stores/{store_id}/archive?taken_at=` — a store ships a sealed archive.
post.description:
The cloud is a **sink for bytes it cannot read**. It does not open the archive, does not parse
it, and holds no key material for it beyond the wrapped column — the seal happened at the till
precisely so that a store's buyer details ([ADR-0107](../../../docs/adr/0107-the-buyer-is-a-subject.md))
never exist here in plaintext.

What it *does* check is the header: eight magic bytes and a format version, so an obviously
wrong body (a plain database, a truncated download, an HTML error page from a proxy) is refused
at upload instead of discovered at restore. That is a shape check and emphatically not
verification — only the key opens an archive, and the cloud has none.

parameters.name: store_id
parameters.description: The store, a ULID. It must be the credential's own

parameters.name: taken_at
parameters.description: When the store took the archive, in milliseconds since the epoch by its own clock

requestBody.description: The sealed archive's bytes, as `pos-edge archive` writes them. The cloud checks the header and cannot open the rest

200.description: Stored: the archive's `object_key`, `size_bytes` and `sha256`, for the store to log

400.description: store_id is not a ULID, taken_at is not a positive time, or the body is not a store archive

401.description: No credential, or one the cloud does not accept: one answer for every credential problem

403.description: The credential lacks the `read_config` scope, or belongs to another store

413.description: The body is larger than 256 MiB

429.description: Too many requests to the store sync surface: `Retry-After` says when to try again

500.description: The archive's storage key could not be built

503.description: The credential store, or the object store or archive registry, is unavailable

post.summary:
`POST /sync/stores/{store_id}/archive-key` — the key this store seals its archives with, minted
on the first ask.
post.description:
Mint-on-first-ask rather than an admin action, because a store that starts archiving must not
need somebody to have remembered; the console reveals and rotates it afterwards. The mint is
insert-if-absent in one statement ([`ArchiveStore::adopt_key`]), so two tills asking in the same
second get the *same* key rather than two — one of which would be the key to archives nobody
could open.

A `POST` for a value that reads like a `GET`, and deliberately so: the first call has a side
effect that outlives it. A `GET` that mints is one a caching proxy or a browser prefetch may
perform unasked, and the thing it would create here is the key to every archive this store ever
ships.

parameters.name: store_id
parameters.description: The store, a ULID. It must be the credential's own

200.description: `key`: the key this store seals its archives with, minted on the first ask (ADR-0124)

401.description: No credential, or one the cloud does not accept: one answer for every credential problem

403.description: The credential lacks the `read_config` scope, or belongs to another store

429.description: Too many requests to the store sync surface: `Retry-After` says when to try again

500.description: The stored key cannot be opened with the configured secret, or no key could be minted

503.description: The credential store, or the archive registry, is unavailable

post.summary:
`POST /sync/stores/{store_id}/artifact` — hands a store the signed release bytes it decided to
install ([ADR-0088](../../../docs/adr/0088-ota-artifact-hosting.md)).
post.description:
**The cloud is a dumb host.** It stores bytes an operator uploaded and hands them back; it never
signs, and it never verifies the minisign signature. The edge verifies against a trust anchor
baked into its own binary ([ADR-0047](../../../docs/adr/0047-minisign-verification.md),
[ADR-0092](../../../docs/adr/0092-artifact-trust-chain.md)), so a compromised cloud, a swapped
blob or a spoofed host can make an update *fail* — never make a box install code.

**`read_config`, the owner's call (2026-09-04).** Every provisioned box already carries that
scope, so the OTA path works with no re-provisioning; a dedicated `fetch_update` scope would be
cleaner and would cost a visit to every live store before a single update could ship. The scope
is here to stop the VPS being an open binary-distribution host, not to keep a signed artifact
secret.

The signature rides `X-Pos-Artifact-Signature` as lowercase hex and the body stays the raw
artifact: a JSON envelope would mean encoding tens of megabytes to carry a few hundred bytes. The
blob holds **raw** signature bytes — ADR-0092 Correction 2 put minisign's base64 decode at the
`/admin` upload, once, under operator supervision, so the edge never sees base64 for a signature.

parameters.name: store_id
parameters.description: The store, a ULID. It must be the credential's own

requestBody.description: `release`, the release tag, and `arch`, the target the store runs

200.description: The release's binary as `application/octet-stream`, its detached signature in the `X-Pos-Artifact-Signature` header as lowercase hex (ADR-0092). The edge verifies both before it installs anything

400.description: store_id is not a ULID, or release or arch is not well formed

401.description: No credential, or one the cloud does not accept: one answer for every credential problem

403.description: The credential lacks the `read_config` scope, or belongs to another store

404.description: The cloud hosts no artifact for that release on that target

429.description: Too many requests to the store sync surface: `Retry-After` says when to try again

500.description: The release is recorded but its binary or signature is missing, the stored binary does not match its recorded digest, or the signature could not be sent

503.description: The credential store, or the release registry or artifact store, is unavailable

get.summary:
Serves a store its own configuration update: nothing (up to date), a delta, or a full snapshot
past *K* versions behind ([ADR-0039](../../../docs/adr/0039-config-delivery.md)).
get.description:
Requires a valid API key with the `read_config` scope, and answers **only** for that key's tenant:
the tenant comes from the verified grant, never the path, so a store can pull a `store_id` only
within its own tenant. A store outside the tenant, or one with nothing published, reads `404`.

parameters.name: store_id
parameters.description: The store, a ULID. It must be the credential's own

parameters.name: held_version
parameters.description: The config version the store holds, a ULID. Absent when it holds none

200.description: `status`: `up_to_date`, or `update` with the snapshot or collapsed delta that brings the store to the current version (ADR-0039)

400.description: store_id is not a ULID, or held_version is not a ULID

401.description: No credential, or one the cloud does not accept: one answer for every credential problem

403.description: The credential lacks the `read_config` scope, or belongs to another store

404.description: Nothing is published for this store in the credential's tenant

429.description: Too many requests to the store sync surface: `Retry-After` says when to try again

503.description: The credential store, or the configuration service, is unavailable

get.summary:
A store lists its **approved** devices (`manage_devices` scope) — what the edge acts on, never a
raw discovery.

parameters.name: store_id
parameters.description: The store, a ULID. It must be the credential's own

200.description: The store's approved devices, never a raw discovery

401.description: No credential, or one the cloud does not accept: one answer for every credential problem

403.description: The credential lacks the `manage_devices` scope, or belongs to another store

429.description: Too many requests to the store sync surface: `Retry-After` says when to try again

503.description: The credential store, or the device service, is unavailable

post.summary:
A store proposes a discovered device (`manage_devices` scope). Stored `pending` for an operator to
approve; the id is minted here and returned once.

parameters.name: store_id
parameters.description: The store, a ULID. It must be the credential's own

requestBody.description: A device the store discovered: `kind` (`printer` or `kds`), `name` and `address` (ADR-0041)

201.description: Proposed: its `id`, and `status` pending until an operator approves it at the console

400.description: store_id is not a ULID, kind is not a known device kind, or name or address is blank

401.description: No credential, or one the cloud does not accept: one answer for every credential problem

403.description: The credential lacks the `manage_devices` scope, or belongs to another store

429.description: Too many requests to the store sync surface: `Retry-After` says when to try again

503.description: The credential store, or the device service, is unavailable

post.summary:
`POST /sync/stores/{store_id}/events` — a store publishes its own events over HTTPS
([ADR-0143](../../../docs/adr/0143-the-device-credential-syncs-and-events-travel-over-https.md)).
post.description:
Scope `publish_events`, which a box's device credential always carries, and the store in the
path must be the credential's. **Every envelope must name that store**: a batch with any other
store in it is refused whole, so no credential can write another shop's history. Ingest is the
same idempotent, all-or-nothing [`Cloud::ingest`] the NATS cursor uses, so a batch published
twice is stored once and the answer is the whole batch either way.

parameters.name: store_id
parameters.description: The store, a ULID. It must be the credential's own

requestBody.description: `events`: the store's committed event envelopes, oldest first, at most 256 and 4 MiB, each naming this store (ADR-0143)

200.description: `accepted`: how many envelopes the cloud holds, which is the whole batch. Ingest is idempotent, so a batch published twice is stored once

400.description: store_id is not a ULID, the body is not a batch of events, or it carries more than 256

401.description: No credential, or one the cloud does not accept: one answer for every credential problem

403.description: The credential lacks the `publish_events` scope or belongs to another store, or an envelope names another store; the batch is refused whole

413.description: The body is larger than 4 MiB

429.description: Too many requests to the store sync surface: `Retry-After` says when to try again

503.description: The credential store or the event store is unavailable, and nothing was committed

post.summary:
`POST /sync/stores/{store_id}/events/hello` — the protocol negotiation for the HTTPS event link
([ADR-0024](../../../docs/adr/0024-protocol-version-negotiation.md), ADR-0143), run on the cloud's side with
the cloud's own window. Answers `200` with the [`HelloOutcome`](pos_proto::protocol::HelloOutcome)
either way: a refusal is an answer, not an error, and the store keeps trading on it.

parameters.name: store_id
parameters.description: The store, a ULID. It must be the credential's own

requestBody.description: The store's protocol `Hello`, naming this store and the protocol versions it speaks (ADR-0024)

200.description: The negotiation's outcome, an agreed version or a refusal. A refusal is an answer, not an error, and the store keeps trading on it

400.description: store_id is not a ULID, or the body is not a hello

401.description: No credential, or one the cloud does not accept: one answer for every credential problem

403.description: The credential lacks the `publish_events` scope or belongs to another store, or the hello names another store

429.description: Too many requests to the store sync surface: `Retry-After` says when to try again

post.summary:
`POST /sync/stores/{store_id}/heartbeat` — a store's lightweight liveness ping
([ADR-0068](../../../docs/adr/0068-fleet-liveness.md) slice 2). Authenticated with the same scoped
API key the config pull uses (`read_config`), it advances the store's `last_seen_at` and nothing
else, so a store that is up but not currently pulling config (a parked long-poll, a quiet period
between publishes) still registers as online. `204` on success; unlike the config-pull capture,
recording is this request's whole purpose, so a store-write failure is a `503` the edge retries,
not a swallowed best-effort write.

parameters.name: store_id
parameters.description: The store, a ULID. It must be the credential's own

requestBody.description: Optional: `outbox_depth`, `lease_generation` and `print_agents`, each left out when the store cannot say. An empty body is a bare ping

204.description: Recorded: the store's last contact, and what it reported

400.description: store_id is not a ULID, or the body is not a heartbeat report

401.description: No credential, or one the cloud does not accept: one answer for every credential problem

403.description: The credential lacks the `read_config` scope, or belongs to another store

429.description: Too many requests to the store sync surface: `Retry-After` says when to try again

503.description: The credential store, or the configuration service, is unavailable

get.summary: `GET /sync/stores/{store_id}/orders` — the store pulls its pending batch (bounded long-poll).

parameters.name: store_id
parameters.description: The store, a ULID. It must be the credential's own

200.description: The store's pending relayed orders, each with its `queued_id` and the `order`. Held open for a bounded wait while there are none, and empty if none arrives

401.description: No credential, or one the cloud does not accept: one answer for every credential problem

403.description: The credential lacks the `relay_orders` scope, or belongs to another store

429.description: Too many requests to the store sync surface: `Retry-After` says when to try again

503.description: The credential store, or the order queue, is unavailable

parameters.name: store_id
parameters.description: The store, a ULID. It must be the credential's own

requestBody.description: The store's `outcome`: `accepted`, with the store's order id, its total and its queue number where the channel issues one; or `rejected`, with the refusal's `status` and `message`

204.description: Recorded. A repeated acknowledgement also answers 204

400.description: store_id or queued_id is not a ULID

401.description: No credential, or one the cloud does not accept: one answer for every credential problem

403.description: The credential lacks the `relay_orders` scope, or belongs to another store

429.description: Too many requests to the store sync surface: `Retry-After` says when to try again

503.description: The credential store, or the order queue, is unavailable

post.summary: `POST /sync/stores/{store_id}/reconcile` — the **store's** door onto the same diff.
post.description:
Identity comes from the scoped key the box presents, not from a body it writes: the tenant is the
grant's and the store is the path's, checked against the key's binding. That is the same shape the
config pull, the heartbeat and the OTA report have, and it is why this route needs no shared
secret — a store cannot reach the cloud's private network, and never could
(production-readiness **R3**).

parameters.name: store_id
parameters.description: The store, a ULID. It must be the credential's own

requestBody.description: `event_ids`: the ids of events the store holds, each a ULID

200.description: `missing`: the ids the cloud does not hold, for the store to publish again

400.description: store_id is not a ULID, or an event id is not a ULID

401.description: No credential, or one the cloud does not accept: one answer for every credential problem

403.description: The credential lacks the `read_config` scope, or belongs to another store

429.description: Too many requests to the store sync surface: `Retry-After` says when to try again

503.description: The credential store, or the reconciliation store, is unavailable

post.summary:
Records one store's OTA report ([ADR-0078](../../../docs/adr/0078-sync-and-ota-closure.md)).
Internal (the reporting partner of `/internal/ingest`), so it is absent from the public OpenAPI
and requires the `X-Pos-Internal-Key` shared secret
([ADR-0097](../../../docs/adr/0097-internal-route-authentication.md)) on top of the proxy denies.
A malformed id or an empty version is a `400`; a store failure is a retryable `503`; success is
`204`. The key does not make the report *attributable* — the store id rides in the body — which is
A **store** reports the version it is running, on the route that can say who it is.
post.description:
The tenant comes from the scoped key and the store from the path, so a report is
tenant-attributable — which the `/internal` shape could not be at any strength of secret, because
it read both out of the body ([ADR-0097](../../../docs/adr/0097-internal-route-authentication.md)).

**What this does not close.** A [`Grant`](crate::auth::apikey::Grant) pins a tenant, not a store,
so a key issued to one store can still name a sibling store of the *same tenant* in the path.
That is a real residual and it is stated rather than glossed: the move closes cross-tenant
forgery, not intra-tenant. It is bounded by what a report *is* — pure telemetry that never changes
what any box runs (ADR-0078) — so the worst outcome is a distorted rollout picture for one
operator's own fleet. Closing it needs a store-scoped grant, which is a key-issuance change and
its own slice.

Gated on `read_config`, for the reason [`serve_ota_artifact`] is: every provisioned box already
carries it, so the OTA path works with no re-provisioning, and a report is not a secret.

parameters.name: store_id
parameters.description: The store, a ULID. It must be the credential's own

requestBody.description: `installed`, the release the store now runs, and `self_test_passed` where it has run its post-install self-test (ADR-0078)

400.description: store_id is not a ULID, or installed is blank

401.description: No credential, or one the cloud does not accept: one answer for every credential problem

403.description: The credential lacks the `read_config` scope, or belongs to another store

429.description: Too many requests to the store sync surface: `Retry-After` says when to try again

503.description: The credential store, or the fleet store, is unavailable

AcceptanceRecord.description: A serializable [`OrderAcceptance`] — what the store reports and the relay records and replays.

awaiting_staff_confirmation.description: Whether staff must confirm before the kitchen sees it.

created.description: Whether the store's call created it (vs an idempotent repeat).

queue_number.description: The queue number, for a channel that issues one.

repriced.description: Whether the store's price differed from the caller's quote.

ArchiveAcceptedResponse.description: What the cloud recorded, echoed so a store can log what it shipped.

ArchiveKeyResponse.description: The key a store seals with, as it comes back over `/sync`.

ArtifactRequest.description:
What a store asks for: a release tag, and the architecture it runs.

`arch` is the additive field [ADR-0088](../../../docs/adr/0088-ota-artifact-hosting.md)
Correction 2 added. R1's workflow cross-compiles two targets, so a request without one cannot say
which binary it means — and guessing would hand an `aarch64` box an `x86_64` executable that fails
its self-test after the install, which is the expensive place to find out.

BrandId.description: A `BrandId`: a ULID, 26 Crockford base-32 characters

BusinessDate.description: A business date, YYYY-MM-DD, by the store's own cutoff

ChainHash.description:
A chain hash, as 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters.

A string rather than `[u8; 32]` because it crosses the wire inside the envelope and is
read by humans in a diagnostic; the cost is 32 bytes a record, and the benefit is that
a chain break can be pasted into a bug report.

ChainLink.description:
Where a record sits in its store's chain.

`seq` is a per-store counter starting at one, with no gaps — and it, not `event_id`, is
what orders the chain ([ADR-0131](../../../docs/adr/0131-a-chained-event-log.md)
decision 6). Events sort by ULID elsewhere, and
[ADR-0026](../../../docs/adr/0026-port-shapes.md) §3 already records why that is unsafe
as a cursor once writers are concurrent: a chain built on ULID order would re-link
itself the first time two transactions interleaved.

prev_hash.description: The hash of the record before it, or [`ChainHash::genesis`] for the first.

seq.description: This record's position in its store's chain. The first record is one.

ClaimPending.description: What collecting a claim nobody has bound yet answers: that it is pending.

CollectClaimRequest.description: A box presents its secret to collect.

CollectedClaim.description: What a collection answers once: the box's slot and its device credential.

credential.description: The `posdev_<id>_<secret>` token, shown this once; only its hash is kept.

ConfigDelta.description:
A change from one version to the next.

`from_config_version_id` is what makes a delta safe to apply: a store holding a
different version must reject it rather than apply it out of order, because
configuration is a tree and an out-of-order patch produces a document nobody
authored.

from_config_version_id.description: The version this delta expects the store to be holding.

patch.description: The change, in whatever patch format P7 settles on.

to_config_version_id.description: The version the store reaches by applying it.

ConfigDocument.description: Free-form JSON: a configuration document, or a patch to one, keyed by config node. The port carries it uninterpreted, so a store keeps keys it does not know. Each node's shape is its `pos-proto` type

ConfigSnapshot.description: A complete configuration document at a version.

oneOf.description: The store already holds the current version; it applies nothing.
The store should apply this snapshot or delta.

update.description: The snapshot or collapsed delta to apply ([ADR-0033](../../../docs/adr/0033-config-tree.md)).

ConfigSyncResponse.description:
What a store should do to reach the current configuration — the wire form of a
[`SyncOutcome`](crate::config_tree::SyncOutcome).

allOf.description: Replace everything. Always applicable, whatever version the store holds.

oneOf.description: Replace everything. Always applicable, whatever version the store holds.

allOf.description: Patch forward by one version. Applicable only from the stated version.

oneOf.description: Patch forward by one version. Applicable only from the stated version.

ConfigVersionId.description: A `ConfigVersionId`: a ULID, 26 Crockford base-32 characters

DeviceId.description: A `DeviceId`: a ULID, 26 Crockford base-32 characters

DeviceProposalStatus.description: Where a proposal sits in the approval workflow.

DeviceProposalSummary.description: A proposal as listed — the durable facts plus its status.

agent_device_id.description:
The `terminal` device whose transport reaches this printer, if an operator has picked one
([ADR-0112](../../../docs/adr/0112-print-agents.md)). `None` — the ordinary case — means the
edge opens the address itself, exactly as it always has.

connection.description:
How the device is attached (`usb`/`network`/`serial`), as approval recorded it — `None` while
pending, because discovery cannot find this out ([ADR-0100](../../../docs/adr/0100-receipt-and-ticket-printing.md)).

cuts_paper.description:
Whether an operator says this printer cuts its paper. `None` until somebody says, which the
edge reads as `true`.

drawer_attached.description:
Whether an operator has marked a cash drawer as wired to this printer
([ADR-0165](../../../docs/adr/0165-cash-paid-in-and-out-is-counted-in-the-drawer-and-a-no-sale-opening-needs-a-manager.md)).
`false` until somebody does, which is what every store assumed before the mark existed.

opening_float_minor.description:
On a `terminal`, the float an operator says this till's drawer opens with by default, in the
store currency's minor unit
([ADR-0167](../../../docs/adr/0167-a-till-has-its-own-cash-drawer.md) decision 4). `None`
until somebody says, which is the store's `shift.opening_float_minor`.

paper_width.description:
The paper an operator says this printer takes, as its wire token (`PAPER_WIDTH_…`,
[ADR-0160](../../../docs/adr/0160-everything-a-store-runs-differently-is-published-configuration.md)
decision 2). `None` until somebody says, which the edge reads as 80 mm paper: what every
store assumed before the field existed.

receipt_language.description:
On a `terminal`, the language an operator says this till's receipts print in, as its wire
token (`RECEIPT_LANGUAGE_…`). `None` until somebody says, which is the store's.

receipt_printer_id.description:
On a `terminal`, the printer an operator says this till's receipts, receipt copies and
pre-bills go to (a ULID string,
[ADR-0160](../../../docs/adr/0160-everything-a-store-runs-differently-is-published-configuration.md)
decision 4). `None` until somebody says, which is the store's receipt printer.

receipt_second_language.description:
On a `terminal`, the second language an operator says this till's receipts print in, as its
wire token (`RECEIPT_SECOND_LANGUAGE_…`). `None` until somebody says, which is the store's.

station_id.description:
The kitchen station this device serves, as approval recorded it. `None` for the counter's
receipt printer, which serves the bill rather than a station — and `None` while pending.

store_id.description: The store the device belongs to (a ULID string).

version.description:
The version the row was read at, for a conditional write
([ADR-0094](../../../docs/adr/0094-console-optimistic-concurrency.md)). Opaque: the adapter
mints it from `xmin::text`, and nothing above this seam may assume that.

EmployeeId.description: A `EmployeeId`: a ULID, 26 Crockford base-32 characters

ErrorBody.description: The error body — the schema mirror of [`pos_proto::error::ErrorBody`].

code.description: The HTTP status code, repeated here so a body is self-describing once logged.

details.description: Field-level detail. Absent when the failure is not about a particular field.

message.description: A human-readable explanation. Never contains personal data, because responses are logged.

ErrorDetail.description:
One reason a request failed, tied to the field responsible — the schema mirror of
[`pos_proto::error::ErrorDetail`].

field.description:
The offending field, in the same `snake_case` name the request used. For a whole-request
fault this can be a header name (`if-match`) rather than a body field.

reason.description:
A stable, machine-readable reason such as `MUST_BE_POSITIVE` or `INVALID_ENUM_VALUE`. Stable
so a client can branch on it; `message` is for people and may be reworded at any time.

ErrorResponse.description:
The envelope every `/admin` failure carries — the schema mirror of
[`pos_proto::error::ErrorResponse`].

One level of nesting so a response is unambiguous at the top level: a success body is the record,
a failure body is `{"error": …}`.

EventEnvelope_RawPayload.description:
The envelope carried by every event, on every channel.

`D` is the payload: [`RawPayload`] on receipt, a typed value after decoding.

`PartialEq` is derived rather than hand-written, so comparing two envelopes compares
their payloads by whatever rule `D` defines. For [`RawPayload`] that is a textual
comparison of the JSON — see that type's implementation, which explains why it is not
semantic.

business_date.description:
The trading day it belongs to.

Not derivable from `event_time` alone: it needs the store's timezone and
cut-off hour, both of which are configuration and both of which change. So it
is computed **once, at capture, on the device** and carried here. Recomputing
it downstream would silently rewrite history the next time a store's cut-off
was edited.

oneOf.description:
Where this record sits in its store's hash chain, or `None` for one written before
the chain existed ([ADR-0131](../../../docs/adr/0131-a-chained-event-log.md)).

Additive, and `None` is a real answer rather than a defect: a store's chain begins
at its first record after the migration, and everything earlier verifies as
**unchained** rather than as broken. Backfilling would compute a chain over history
nobody can vouch for, which is the false confidence the record rejects.

It rides on the envelope rather than in a store's own columns so that it crosses
every channel the envelope does — a cloud reader verifies the same bytes the store
wrote, instead of taking the store's word for its own integrity.

data.description:
An event payload exactly as it arrived, still undecoded.

Holding the original bytes is what lets a node forward, store, checksum and
reconcile an event whose payload contains fields it has never heard of. Decoding
eagerly and re-encoding would silently drop them.

oneOf.description:
The member of staff responsible, when there is one.

Absent for system-originated events: a published configuration version, a
completed device activation, a fleet rollout. The envelope's *shape* is still
identical on every channel; this field is simply optional.

event_id.description:
A ULID, which **doubles as the receiver's idempotency key**.

A retry must reuse it. If a command minted a fresh identifier on each attempt,
at-least-once delivery would become at-least-once *effect*, and a bill could be
settled twice. That is why a command carries a caller-supplied request
identifier which becomes this value.

schema_version.description:
The payload contract version for this `event_type`.

Increases only when a break is unavoidable. Adding an optional field does not
bump it — that is what "additive" means.

oneOf.description: The cash shift, when the event occurred inside one.

EventId.description: A `EventId`: a ULID, 26 Crockford base-32 characters

EventTypeRef.description: An event type's dotted name, as the event catalogue writes it

ExchangeRequest.description: A device presents its activation code. Unauthenticated: the code is the credential.

code.description:
The `XXXX-XXXX-XXXX` code the operator typed, in any casing or spacing, with or without its
cell's prefix (`VN1-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX`, ADR-0181). Only its twelve symbols are looked up.

store_id.description:
The store the box was installed for, from its `config.toml`. A code issued for another store
is refused before it is spent. Optional, because an edge older than the field sends none.

ExchangeResponse.description: The device's minted credential and the device id it was activated as — shown once.

credential.description: The `posdev_<id>_<secret>` bearer token the device stores in its `KeyVault`.

device_id.description: The device id the credential authenticates as.

HeartbeatBody.description:
What a heartbeat may carry beyond "I am here" ([ADR-0068](../../../docs/adr/0068-fleet-liveness.md)).

Every field is optional and the whole body is optional, because the body is younger than the
route: a store running an older binary posts nothing at all, and must keep being recorded as
alive rather than refused for sending the empty body it has always sent.

lease_generation.description:
The lease generation the box holds
([ADR-0108](../../../docs/adr/0108-the-lease-generation-is-authority.md)), so the console can
tell a store that has been *replaced* from one that is merely quiet. `None` when the store did
not say — an older edge, or one whose lease row could not be read — and that must not be
recorded as `0`, because `0` is a store's real first generation.

outbox_depth.description:
How many events the store has committed and not yet published — its own publish backlog, the
opposite direction from the relay backlog the fleet row already carries. `None` when the store
did not say, which is a different answer from zero and leaves the recorded depth alone.

print_agents.description:
One standing per bound print agent ([ADR-0112](../../../docs/adr/0112-print-agents.md)), or
`None` when the store said nothing about them — an older edge, or one whose record could not
be read.

The distinction between absent and empty is load-bearing and is why this is not a bare
`Vec`. Absent leaves whatever the cloud last knew alone. Empty says *this store has no bound
agent*, which a manager releasing the last terminal produces and which must replace the
stored list — a console still showing an agent nobody is bound to is the stale answer this
field exists to prevent.

Hello.description: The first frame a store sends on connecting.

oneOf.description:
The lease this machine holds, when it has one.

Absent during activation, before a lease has been issued.

product_version.description:
The edge's product release.

**It does not reach the fleet view** (production-readiness **R2**). There are two production
[`MessageLink`](pos_ports::message_link::MessageLink)s, and neither records it:

- `link-nats` is outbound-only by design
  ([ADR-0089](../../../docs/adr/0089-edge-event-bus-transport.md)). There is no cloud responder,
  so its `handshake` runs [`negotiate`] against its *own* compiled constants and this field is
  never transmitted.
- `cloud-sync-http`'s link
  ([ADR-0143](../../../docs/adr/0143-the-device-credential-syncs-and-events-travel-over-https.md))
  posts this frame to the cloud, which negotiates the version range against its own and reads
  nothing else from it.

The console learns which binary a store runs from
[`CloudSync::report`](pos_ports::cloud_sync::CloudSync::report) over `/sync`
([ADR-0078](../../../docs/adr/0078-sync-and-ota-closure.md)), which is a different rail.

The field stays because the frame is the protocol's, not one transport's, and removing a
member from a wire type is a `PROTOCOL_VERSION` change made for no gain.

protocol_version_max.description: The newest protocol version this edge can speak.

protocol_version_min.description: The oldest protocol version this edge can speak.

oneOf.description: Agreed. Both sides speak this version for the life of the connection.

protocol_version.description: The negotiated version: the highest both sides support.

oneOf.description:
No overlap.

The edge keeps selling, keeps its outbox, backs off, and raises the condition.
It does **not** retry in a tight loop, and it does not stop trading.

maximum_supported.description: The newest version the cloud speaks.

minimum_supported.description: The oldest version the cloud speaks, so the edge can report what it needs.

LeaseToken.description:
An opaque proof that a machine is the single active server for its store.

Carried on the handshake so single-active enforcement and version negotiation share
one round trip ([ADR-0003](../../../docs/adr/0003-cattle-not-pets.md)).

`Debug` redacts the value. A lease token in a log line is a credential in a log line,
and logs travel to the cloud.

MoneyPayload.description: A money value on the wire.

amount_minor.description: The amount in the currency's minor unit.

OpenedClaim.description: What `POST /claim` answers. The box shows `user_code` and keeps `secret` to itself.

secret.description: 256 bits, as hex. Shown nowhere; presented only to collect.

PendingOrderDto.description: One pending order on the wire, for the pull response.

PendingStatus.description: The one status a pending claim answers with.

PrintAgentStanding.description:
One bound print agent, as the store last reported it
([ADR-0112](../../../docs/adr/0112-print-agents.md)).

Ids are kept as raw strings for the reason the config versions below are: the cloud did not mint
the paired device id — the store did — and one report the cloud cannot parse must not fail a
whole fleet read. The console shows what the store said.

Carries no personal data by construction: two opaque identifiers and a duration. Nothing a ticket
*says* helps diagnose a stalled agent, so nothing a ticket says is here.

agent_device_id.description: The terminal a console admin created and a manager bound at the till.

oldest_unacknowledged_secs.description:
How long the oldest still-unacknowledged job has waited, or `None` when nothing is waiting.

`None` is the healthy answer and is deliberately not zero: an agent with an empty queue and
one whose ticket arrived this instant are different states, and only one is about to become
an alert.

paired_device_id.description: The paired device answering for it.

ProposeDeviceRequest.description: A store's proposal of a discovered device.

address.description: The device's network address, as discovered (e.g. `192.168.1.50:9100`).

name.description: A human-readable name for the device.

ProposeDeviceResponse.description: The id and status of a freshly-proposed device (always `pending`).

status.description: The status — `pending` until an operator resolves it.

PublishedEvents.description: `POST /sync/stores/{store_id}/events`'s body: the store's committed events, oldest first.

PublishedEventsAccepted.description:
What a publish came to: how many envelopes, counted from the first, the cloud holds. Always the
whole batch on success, since ingest commits all of it or none (ADR-0143).

note.description: The guest's free-text note; stays at the store, never the event log.

quoted_unit_price.description: The price the caller quoted, advisory only.

QueuedOrderPayload.description:
A queued order's payload, in a serializable wire form — what the queue stores and the store pulls.
The domain [`InboundOrder`] is not `Serialize` (its `GuestNote` cannot enter the event log), so
the relay carries this explicit shape; the guest note rides along to the store here (this is order
delivery, not the log) and never touches the event stream.

external_reference.description: The caller's reference — the idempotency key, scoped by channel.

placed_at_ms.description: When the caller says it was placed (ms since the Unix epoch).

sales_channel.description: The channel the order arrived on (an open enum's wire token).

subject_id.description: The recipient side-table id, when there is one.

table_id.description: The table, for a QR order.

ReconcileResponse.description: The ids the cloud is missing from the manifest — what the edge should re-push.

missing.description: The subset of the manifest the cloud's event log does not contain (ULID strings).

ReleaseTag.description:
A release identifier, such as `v1.4.0`.

Admissible in an event payload: it names a build, not a person. Fleet rollout
events carry it so the dashboard can show which store runs which version.

ShiftId.description: A `ShiftId`: a ULID, 26 Crockford base-32 characters

StoreId.description: A `StoreId`: a ULID, 26 Crockford base-32 characters

allOf.description: The store accepted (or idempotently matched) the order.

oneOf.description: The store accepted (or idempotently matched) the order.

The store refused it — an unknown item, a closed store, a rate limit. `status` is the
[`pos_proto::error::ErrorStatus`] wire name so the caller sees the same class the port defines.

StoreOutcome.description: What a store reported for a pulled order: an acceptance, or a refusal it decided locally.

StoreReconcileRequest.description:
A store's own reconciliation manifest: just the ids, because the tenant and the store come from
the key it presented and the path it called (production-readiness **R3**).

Deliberately **not** [`ReconcileRequest`] with two ignored members: a body that carries a
`tenant_id` the server discards is a body a caller will eventually believe is honoured.

event_ids.description: The event ids this store holds over the window it is reconciling.

StoreReportRequest.description:
What a **store** reports about itself ([ADR-0078](../../../docs/adr/0078-sync-and-ota-closure.md)),
on the `/sync` route that replaced the `/internal` one for store-originated reporting
([ADR-0097](../../../docs/adr/0097-internal-route-authentication.md)).

No `tenant_id` and no `store_id`: the tenant comes from the scoped key and the store from the
path. That is the entire point of the move — the `/internal` shape took both in the body, so it
trusted the caller's claim about which store it was, and a shared secret could change *who could
reach* the route without making a report attributable.

installed.description: The release the store is now running.

self_test_passed.description:
Whether the post-install self-test passed; absent when the store has never self-tested
(ADR-0078 Amendment 1).

base_url.description: That cell's origin. Null only when it is this cell and its base URL is not configured.

here.description: Whether that cell is this one.

TenantId.description: A `TenantId`: a ULID, 26 Crockford base-32 characters

Timestamp.description: An instant in UTC, as RFC 3339

WellKnownCell.description: This cell, as anyone may know it.

base_url.description: The origin this cell answers on. Null when it is not configured.

cell_id.description: This cell's id (`vn1`), or `default` for a cloud with no `[cell]` section.

country_alias.description: This cell's country alias (`vn`), when one is configured.

directory_version.description: The version of the signed directory this cell answers from. Null when it holds none.

home_country.description: The country this cell's tenants are homed by. Null when it is not configured.

tenant.description: The asked-for tenant's home. Present only when `tenant` was asked.

device_credential.description: A box's device credential, issued once by `/activate` or a collected claim, or its store's scoped API key, presented as a bearer token. Each requirement's role is the scope the route checks, and the credential answers only for its own store.

tags.name: configuration
tags.description: The store's published configuration, pulled as a snapshot or a delta, and its liveness heartbeat (ADR-0039, ADR-0068).

tags.name: events
tags.description: The store's own events, published over HTTPS after a protocol hello, and the reconciliation that finds what the cloud is missing (ADR-0143, ADR-0024, ADR-0078).

tags.name: order relay
tags.description: Orders taken for the store elsewhere, pulled by a bounded long-poll and acknowledged with the store's outcome (ADR-0061).

tags.name: updates
tags.description: The signed release a store installs, and what it reports once it runs it (ADR-0088, ADR-0078).

tags.name: archives
tags.description: The key a store seals its archives with, and the sealed archives it ships, which the cloud cannot open (ADR-0124).

tags.name: devices
tags.description: Printers and kitchen displays a store discovers and proposes, and the ones an operator approved (ADR-0041).

tags.name: box activation
tags.description: How a box first comes to hold its device credential: an activation code from the setup sheet, or a claim the console binds (ADR-0050, ADR-0148).

tags.name: cells
tags.description: Which cell this cloud is, and which cell is a tenant's home, from the signed, PII-free cell directory. Asked once by a box being set up, which then keeps its `cloud_url` (ADR-0179).
